title: Compare tokens without leaking where they differ

blocks.text: `String.equals` returns at the first character that differs, so the time it takes tells an attacker **where** the first mismatch is, and a token can be guessed one character at a time. The page's constant-time comparison **never returns at the first differing character**: it combines the differences of all characters (`result |= a ^ b`) and decides only at the end. Returning early on different **lengths** is acceptable, since token lengths are public.

items: `true` exactly when both hold the same characters;
when the lengths are equal, it reads **every** character of `given`, wherever the first mismatch is;

cases.says: tok-4f9a2c matches itself (built at run time) and not tok-4f9a2d.
Comparing tokens that differ at the first or the fifth character still reads all 10 characters of the given token.
Tokens that differ only in their first or their ninth character do not match.
A prefix of the token, the token plus one character, and the empty string do not match.
A null given token does not match.

concepts: Security tokens are compared in constant time, never returning at the first differing character; an early return on length leaks only the public length.
